responses.title: Upscale South Kensington Nightlife & Dining Guide
responses.description: Editorial guides to refined South Kensington nightlife, sushi dining, cocktails, shisha lounges, live events and day-to-night experiences in West London.

links.text: Case Study: Turning a Graduation Brunch into a Polished Day-to-Night Celebration Live Music & Events 28 Aug Imogen Sterling
The Smart Reservation Guide for South Kensington Dining: Tables, Timings and Group Etiquette Cocktails & Bars 21 Aug Eleanor Whitworth
Omakase, À La Carte or Late Supper: Choosing the Right Japanese Dining Format Before a Night Out Brunch 14 Aug Lorenzo Moretti
Last Entry, Re-Entry and Queue Priority: The Club Rules That Catch People Out Sushi & Dining 07 Aug Imogen Sterling
What Makes South Kensington Busy After Dark? A Data-Led Look at Seasons, Students and Events South Kensington Nightlife 31 Jul Layla Mansour
The South Kensington Night-Out Timing Guide: When to Dine, Drink, Arrive and Leave South Kensington Nightlife 24 Jul Kieran O’Sullivan
Guest Lists, Table Minimums and Door Spend: How Upscale Club Entry Really Works South Kensington Nightlife 17 Jul Alistair Thorne
London Club Dress Codes Explained: What Smart Casual Really Means South Kensington Nightlife 12 Jun Imogen Sterling
South Kensington Nightlife Clubbing, late-night venues, dress codes and guest lists across the upscale West London scene.
Sushi & Dining Sushi counters, evening dining and the kind of pre-club meal that sets up the rest of the night.
Cocktails & Bars Drinks menus, lounge ambience and the early-evening rooms worth arriving at first.
Brunch Weekend dining, bottomless tables and celebratory brunches that stretch into evening.
Live Music & Events Venue programming, DJ nights, ticketed events and London's event-going culture.
Shisha Lounges Hookah culture, etiquette and the relaxed late-night settings that close a night gently.

Sushi, small plates and social dining
brunch styles for a London weekend

<section class="crki-partition">
 <div class="crki-stage">
 
 <p>This is an editorial guide, not a directory. We write for people who want a night that holds together: a proper dinner, the right drink in hand, and a final venue that matches the mood rather than fighting it. Whether you're a local who's seen it all or a visitor planning one memorable evening, the goal is the same — a refined day-to-night experience that feels deliberate.</p>
 </div>
</section>

<section class="crki-partition">
 <div class="crki-stage">
 <h2 id="planning-a-night-that-actually-flows">Planning a Night That Actually Flows</h2>
 <p>The difference between a decent evening and a great one usually comes down to sequence. Order matters. A heavy bottomless brunch doesn't pair well with a club entry around 1am, and a sushi-led dinner sits far better before cocktails than after them.</p>
 <p>Start with the anchor — the meal, the gig, or the table you've committed to, then build outward. If live music is the centrepiece, our guide on <a href="/live-music-events/how-to-plan-a-night-around-live-music-dinner-and-drinks/">planning a night around live music, dinner and drinks</a> walks through the timing without overthinking it. Building around food instead? <a href="/sushi-dining/sushi-small-plates-and-social-dining-a-london-nightlife/">Sushi, small plates and social dining</a> covers how a shared-plate format keeps a group loose before the night ramps up.</p>
 <div class="crki-grant-block">
 <p class="crki-module-head">Field Note:</p>
 <p>Decide your last venue first. Knowing whether you're ending on a dancefloor or in a shisha lounge shapes every earlier choice — dress code, drink pace, how late you eat. Our piece on <a href="/shisha-lounges/shisha-lounge-cocktail-bar-or-club-choosing-the-right-late/">choosing the right late-night atmosphere</a> is the place to start that call.</p>
 </div>
 <p>Cocktails deserve their own thought too. A well-built classic holds up late, and <a href="/cocktails-bars/classic-cocktails-that-suit-a-late-night-london-setting/">our rundown of late-night classics</a> leans toward drinks that stay balanced as the evening wears on. For weekends, <a href="/brunch/best-brunch-styles-for-a-london-weekend-classic-bottomless/">brunch styles for a London weekend</a> sorts the celebratory from the leisurely.</p>
 </div>
</section>

                <p class="crki-text">A day-to-night graduation brunch is a coordinated sequence of brunch, cocktails, dinner and late-night plans, arranged around changing guest numbers and energy levels. The format preserves the momentum of graduation day without asking every relative, friend and coursemate to commit to the full programme.</p>
<p class="crki-text">This South Kensington case model divides the celebration into four phases across an illustrative 12-to-14-hour window. Any example times below are planning examples rather than records of a completed event. The value lies in the structure: each phase has its own guest list, booking pressure and cost model.</p>


<p class="crki-text"><strong>Table of Contents</strong></p>
<ol class="crki-list--numbered">
<li class="crki-list-pip"><a href="#graduation-format">What a Day-to-Night Graduation Brunch Means</a></li>
<li class="crki-list-pip"><a href="#guest-list">The Guest List Forced an Early Decision</a></li>
<li class="crki-list-pip"><a href="#venue-sequence">Building the South Kensington Venue Sequence</a></li>
<li class="crki-list-pip"><a href="#run-sheet">The Run Sheet That Held the Day Together</a></li>
<li class="crki-list-pip"><a href="#hosted-costs">Separating Hosted Costs from Guest Spending</a></li>
<li class="crki-list-pip"><a href="#four-phase-outcome">What Changed in the Four-Phase Plan</a></li>
<li class="crki-list-pip"><a href="#lock-dinner">Lock the Dinner Before Announcing the Day</a></li>
</ol>

<section id="graduation-format">
<h2 class="crki-subheading">What a Day-to-Night Graduation Brunch Means</h2>
<p class="crki-text">The central planning problem is stamina. Graduation ceremonies, photographs and family logistics already demand attention before the first glass reaches the table. Turning the celebration into a single marathon reservation places unnecessary pressure on guests who have different travel plans, budgets and ideas of a good night out.</p>
<p class="crki-text">The planning team therefore mapped the day as an energy arc. Brunch carried the formal graduation moment. Cocktails created space for arrivals and departures. Dinner brought the confirmed evening group together, while the late-night booking served guests who still wanted music and a livelier atmosphere.</p>
<h3 class="crki-h3">Four moods, one celebration</h3>
<p class="crki-text">Each phase had a distinct job:</p>
<ul class="crki-list">
<li class="crki-list-pip"><strong>Brunch</strong> hosted the graduate, close family and key friends around a seated meal.</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip"><strong>Afternoon cocktails</strong> opened the group to flexible joiners without forcing an exact arrival minute.</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip"><strong>Dinner</strong> established the firmest headcount and the most controlled seating plan.</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip"><strong>Late night</strong> shifted the focus towards south kensington nightlife, music and optional table service.</li>
</ul>
<p class="crki-text">That modular shape gives the day rhythm. It also lets an aunt leave after cocktails, a former flatmate arrive for dinner and a larger friendship group join later without making anyone feel as though they attended the wrong portion.</p>
<blockquote class="crki-excerpt">
<p class="crki-text"><strong>Protect The Peak</strong></p>
<p class="crki-text">Choose the one phase that carries the emotional weight of the graduation. Host and photograph that moment properly, then let the remaining plans become progressively more flexible.</p>
</blockquote>
</section>
<section id="guest-list">
<h2 class="crki-subheading">The Guest List Forced an Early Decision</h2>
<p class="crki-text">A single all-day reservation looked simple on paper. In practice, it would have tied graduates, relatives, friends and late-night guests to the same schedule. The guest list became workable only when attendance was treated as a set of planning categories rather than one fixed social group.</p>
<h3 class="crki-h3">Four ways to attend</h3>
<ul class="crki-list">
<li class="crki-list-pip"><strong>Brunch guests:</strong> the hosted core, usually requiring confirmed seats, dietary details and accessibility checks.</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip"><strong>Afternoon joiners:</strong> guests who can arrive during a wider cocktail window and may stay for only one drink.</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip"><strong>Dinner confirmations:</strong> the precise headcount supplied to the restaurant by its stated deadline.</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip"><strong>Late-night attendees:</strong> guests whose access may depend on advance booking, age restrictions, dress code, last entry or door policy.</li>
</ul>
<p class="crki-text">These categories describe participation, not importance. Clear labels simply stop a flexible cocktail RSVP from being mistaken for a guaranteed dinner seat.</p>
<p class="crki-text">Dinner drove the first serious decision because a restaurant needs a reliable number for table allocation, deposits and dietary arrangements. The planning window allowed roughly three to four weeks to collect dietary and accessibility requirements. That gave the organiser time to chase missing replies before the venue’s own cut-off.</p>
<p class="crki-text">Cocktails could absorb looser arrivals, especially where the chosen bar accepted a reserved area or a controlled walk-in group. The late-night phase needed a different kind of certainty. A guest saying “maybe later” carries little operational value when a venue requires names, tickets or a table commitment.</p>
<blockquote class="crki-excerpt">
<p class="crki-text"><strong>RSVP With Purpose</strong></p>
<p class="crki-text">Ask each guest to confirm specific phases. One message with four clear choices produces a cleaner answer than an open invitation to “join at some point”.</p>
</blockquote>
</section>
<section id="venue-sequence">
<h2 class="crki-subheading">Building the South Kensington Venue Sequence</h2>
<p class="crki-text">The sequence was built backwards from dinner. An early attempt to book chronologically, beginning with the morning table, was dropped once strict evening seating times started dictating the entire afternoon.</p>
<p class="crki-text">Dinner has the smallest margin for drift. Once its capacity, seating time and deposit terms are secure, brunch can be placed far enough ahead to feel relaxed and cocktails can fill the middle without threatening check-in.</p>
<h3 class="crki-h3">Operational fit beats a famous postcode</h3>
<p class="crki-text">A polished room can still be wrong for a graduation group. The shortlist needs to cover the details that shape the day:</p>
<ul class="crki-list">
<li class="crki-list-pip">brunch table duration, with two hours used as the standard planning assumption in this case;</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip">bar reservation rules and whether standing arrivals can join gradually;</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip">dinner seating time, minimum spend, service charge and deposit terms;</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip">music level during family conversation and later cocktails;</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip">step-free access, suitable seating and accessible facilities;</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip">dress code, identification requirements and late-night entry conditions.</li>
</ul>
<p class="crki-text">Sushi & dining may suit the evening anchor when the table wants a celebratory menu and a sharper room. A softer brunch setting works better earlier, particularly when family members need time for speeches, dessert and photographs. Cocktails & bars then bridge those two moods.</p>
<h3 class="crki-h3">The continuity test</h3>
<p class="crki-text">Every proposed move was checked against a walking radius of about ten to fifteen minutes. The test also covered weather exposure, coat management, uneven pavements and the likelihood that guests would split into smaller groups along the route.</p>
<p class="crki-text">Graduation clothing changes the calculation. Formal shoes, gowns, flowers and gift bags make a short map distance feel longer. One lead person should know the route and the next venue’s check-in name before the group leaves.</p>
<p class="crki-text">The multi-venue format also has a clear boundary: it becomes difficult to manage when the core family group includes elderly relatives who need one stationary setting throughout. In that situation, a hotel or restaurant with separate dining and lounge spaces offers a sounder base than repeated street-level transfers.</p>
</section>
<section id="run-sheet">
<h2 class="crki-subheading">The Run Sheet That Held the Day Together</h2>
<p class="crki-text">The run sheet avoided back-to-back bookings. It treated bill settlement, photographs, coat retrieval, travel and check-in as scheduled activity rather than invisible minutes that would somehow take care of themselves.</p>
<p class="crki-text">The following matrix is illustrative. Venue deadlines and arrival rules should be replaced with the confirmed terms for the selected date.</p>
<div class="crki-matrix-wrap">
Four-Phase Graduation Planning Matrix
<table class="crki-matrix"><thead>
<tr>
<th>Phase</th>
<th>Arrival Window</th>
<th>Booking Deadline</th>
<th>Cost Model</th>
<th>Fallback Option</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<th>Brunch</th>
<td>11:00 AM–11:15 AM</td>
<td>About three weeks prior</td>
<td>Fully hosted</td>
<td>Nearby unreserved café</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<th>Cocktails</th>
<td>2:30 PM–4:00 PM</td>
<td>Flexible or walk-in</td>
<td>Individual drinks</td>
<td>Second bar within walking radius</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<th>Dinner</th>
<td>Illustrative fixed evening check-in</td>
<td>Venue confirmation deadline</td>
<td>Shared or subsidised</td>
<td>Smaller confirmed table</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<th>Late night</th>
<td>After dinner and before last entry</td>
<td>Door or table-booking deadline</td>
<td>Individual entry or table share</td>
<td>Live music & events bar nearby</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>
<h3 class="crki-h3">Cocktails carried the handover</h3>
<p class="crki-text">The afternoon window acted as the flexible hinge. Brunch guests could finish at their own pace, evening friends could join, and the organiser could complete the final dinner check without interrupting a seated meal.</p>
<p class="crki-text">Three decision gates controlled the headcounts: confirmation before the hosted brunch, final numbers for dinner and a late-night check against entry conditions. Between phases, buffers of around half an hour to forty-five minutes covered payment, coats and movement. That breathing room mattered more than squeezing in another round.</p>
<p class="crki-text">One named person handled each transfer. The organiser settled brunch and signalled the cocktail departure; another guest checked the dinner table; a late-night lead held booking details and understood last entry. Those handovers reduced the chance of twenty people asking the graduate the same logistical question.</p>
<blockquote class="crki-excerpt">
<p class="crki-text"><strong>Buffer The Bills</strong></p>
<p class="crki-text">Never set the next arrival time from the moment food service should end. Start from the realistic point at which the final card payment clears and the last coat is found.</p>
</blockquote>
</section><section id="hosted-costs">
<h2 class="crki-subheading">Separating Hosted Costs from Guest Spending</h2>
<p class="crki-text">The budget became clearer once brunch was defined as the sole hosted graduation milestone. Everything after it moved to a shared, subsidised or individual payment basis, preventing the host from underwriting an open-ended evening.</p>
<h3 class="crki-h3">Costs that need a named owner</h3>
<p class="crki-text">The working budget separated brunch food, drinks, service charge, cake or dessert, deposits, transport, dinner, late-night entry, table commitments and contingency. Each line had an owner and a payment point.</p><figure class="crki-tableau crki-tableau--medium">
<img src="/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/graduation-brunch-day-to-night-celebration-case-study-content-1-e73a0e8.webp" alt="Costs that need a named owner" loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="690" height="420">
</figure>
<p class="crki-text">Deposits deserve particular attention in a multi-venue plan. The case used refund deadlines falling around seven to ten days before the relevant booking as a control point. That gave the organiser room to release unused capacity before the money became exposed, provided the actual venue terms matched that window.</p>
<h3 class="crki-h3">Three payment models</h3>
<ol class="crki-list--numbered">
<li class="crki-list-pip"><strong>Host brunch only.</strong> The invitation states that brunch food and an agreed drinks element are covered. Guests pay for later phases.</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip"><strong>Subsidise selected phases.</strong> The host covers brunch and perhaps a welcome drink at dinner, while guests settle the remainder.</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip"><strong>Set one hosted element.</strong> Guests pay individually after a clearly identified cake, bottle, course or round supplied by the host.</li>
</ol>
<p class="crki-text">The first model suited this case because it gave the family a contained celebratory moment and kept the evening open to guests with different budgets. It also simplified service-charge discussions: brunch had one payer, while later bookings followed their stated split-payment arrangement.</p>
<p class="crki-text">Clarity belongs in the invitation. A guest should know before accepting dinner whether the table will split evenly, pay by item or contribute towards a set menu. The same applies to shisha lounges, club tables and ticketed live music & events, where a casual “join us later” can conceal a significant commitment.</p>
</section>
<section id="four-phase-outcome">
<h2 class="crki-subheading">What Changed in the Four-Phase Plan</h2>
<p class="crki-text">The original idea treated the celebration as one continuous guest list. Four distinct phases replaced it, with three scheduled handover points and separate confirmations wherever a booking required fixed numbers.</p>
<p class="crki-text">That structural change produced practical gains. Dinner capacity became easier to protect because only confirmed diners reached the restaurant list. Guests knew when they could arrive and leave. The organiser moved from active hosting towards passive schedule management as the day progressed.</p>
<h3 class="crki-h3">Fewer decisions during the celebration</h3>
<p class="crki-text">By brunch, the first arrival list was settled. During cocktails, attention shifted to the dinner gate. After dinner, the final check concerned late-night eligibility and entry timing. Each question appeared once, at the point where it could still be acted upon.</p>
<p class="crki-text">The three handovers also gave the day visible changes of pace. Brunch felt intimate and ceremonial. Cocktails loosened the room. Dinner restored focus around a table, then the final move introduced music, dancing or a lounge atmosphere for those continuing.</p>
<p class="crki-text">This is where segmentation earns its place. A graduation party does not need to maintain the same volume for roughly 12 to 14 hours. It needs momentum, and momentum comes from changing the setting before the current one starts to drag.</p>
</section>
<section id="lock-dinner">
<h2 class="crki-subheading">Lock the Dinner Before Announcing the Day</h2>
<p class="crki-text">The booking order follows the pressure points. Choose the dinner date and realistic capacity first. Shortlist a compatible brunch next, identify a flexible cocktail stop within the walking radius, then confirm the late-night option.</p>
<h3 class="crki-h3">The final booking check</h3>
<ul class="crki-list">
<li class="crki-list-pip">Record every deposit and cancellation date.</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip">Collect dietary requirements and accessibility needs within the three-to-four-week planning window.</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip">Confirm the brunch table duration and dinner seating time.</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip">Check age restrictions, identification rules, dress code and last entry.</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip">Ask whether venues permit split bills, cakes, decorations or outside photography.</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip">Map transport and walking routes between all four phases.</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip">Assign an owner to each arrival, deadline and payment decision.</li>
</ul>
<p class="crki-text">A four-row control sheet can track the arrival rule, booking deadline, owner and cost model for every phase. Keep the wider invitation provisional while deposits and restrictive reservations remain unsecured. Once the dinner and any late-night commitment are financially locked, issue one unified itinerary rather than allowing fragments of the plan to circulate through separate chats.</p>
<p class="crki-text">The finished invitation should say exactly what is hosted, where guests may join, which phases demand confirmation and when the final venue admits them. With the dinner table secured, which three phases genuinely deserve a place around it?</p>
</section>

        var delMsg = "Your comment was deleted.";

        function matchesApproved(pendingContent) {

            var storedData = (pendingContent || '').trim().toLowerCase().substring(0, 50);
            if (!storedData) return false;

            for (var i = 0; i < comments.length; i++) {
                var approved = (comments[i].textContent || '').trim().toLowerCase().substring(0, 50);
                if (approved === storedData) return true;
            }
            return false;
        }

        // Show pending comment from localStorage
        function showPendingComment() {
            var storedData = localStorage.getItem(pendingKey);
            if (!storedData) return;

            try {
                var data = JSON.parse(storedData);

                if (matchesApproved(data.comment)) {
                    localStorage.removeItem(pendingKey);
                    return;
                }

                var msgEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-comment-' + postId);
                var nameEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-author-' + postId);
                var payloadEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-content-' + postId);
                var alertEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-warning-' + postId);

                if (msgEl && nameEl && payloadEl) {
                    nameEl.textContent = data.name || "Your comment";
                    payloadEl.textContent = data.comment || '';
                    msgEl.style.display = '';

                    // Show warning in form
                    if (alertEl) alertEl.style.display = '';
                }
            } catch (e) {
                localStorage.removeItem(pendingKey);
            }
        }

        // Load on page ready
        if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
            document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', showPendingComment);
        } else {
            showPendingComment();
        }

        window.clearPending = function(id) {
            // Hide UI immediately
            var msgEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-comment-' + id);
            var alertEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-warning-' + id);
            if (msgEl) msgEl.style.display = 'none';
            if (alertEl) alertEl.style.display = 'none';
            
            // Clear localStorage
            localStorage.removeItem('_dfb_' + id);
            
            // Call API to delete from server
            fetch('/endpoint.php?op=delete_comment', {
                method: 'POST',
                body: new URLSearchParams({ 'item_id': id })
            })
            .then(function(r) { return r.json(); })
            .then(function(result) {
                if (typeof showNotice === 'function') {
                    showNotice(delMsg, 'success');
                }
            })
            .catch(function(err) {
                if (typeof showNotice === 'function') {
                    showNotice(delMsg, 'neutral');
                }
            });
        };

    })();

    (function() {
        var postId = 36;
        var visibleCount = 20;
        var textTemplate = 'Show more comments ({count})';
        var storageKey = '_dfb_' + postId;
        var hasAuth = false;
        var dateLayout = 'header_right';
        var queueState = 'Under Review';
        var holdPfx = 'held';
        var lmPfx = 'showmore';
        var delMsg = "Your comment was deleted.";
        var removedKey = '_ddcl';

        function parseHtml(html) {
            var txt = document.createElement("textarea");
            txt.innerHTML = html;
            return txt.value;
        }
        
        function cleanHtml(str) {
            var div = document.createElement('div');
            div.textContent = str || '';
            return div.innerHTML;
        }

        function getPendingStatus() {
            var stored = localStorage.getItem(storageKey);
            if (!stored) return;
            try {
                var data = JSON.parse(stored);
                var pending = (data.comment || '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim().toLowerCase().substring(0, 50);
                
                // Check if already in server-rendered DOM (exclude JS pending element)
                var inDom = false;
                var comments = document.querySelectorAll('.crki-feedback:not(.crki-feedback--pending) .crki-feedback__content');
                for (var i = 0; i < comments.length; i++) {
                    var domContent = comments[i].textContent.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim().toLowerCase().substring(0, 50);
                    if (domContent === pending) {
                        inDom = true;
                        var article = comments[i].closest('.crki-feedback');
                        if (article && !article.querySelector('.crki-feedback__badge')) {
                            localStorage.removeItem(storageKey);
                        }
                        break;
                    }
                }

                if (!inDom) {
                     var container = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-comment-' + postId);
                     var nameEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-author-' + postId);
                     var payloadEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-content-' + postId);

                     var dateElId = holdPfx + '-date-' + postId;
                     if (dateLayout === 'header_inline') dateElId = holdPfx + '-date-inline-' + postId;
                     if (dateLayout === 'subtitle') dateElId = holdPfx + '-date-sub-' + postId;
                     if (dateLayout === 'footer') dateElId = holdPfx + '-date-foot-' + postId;

                     var dateEl = document.getElementById(dateElId);

                     if (container && nameEl && payloadEl) {
                         nameEl.textContent = data.name || "Your comment";
                         payloadEl.textContent = data.comment || '';
                         if (dateEl) dateEl.textContent = data.date || "Right now";
                         container.style.display = '';
                     }
                } else {
                    // In DOM, hide pending
                     var container = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-comment-' + postId);
                     if (container) container.style.display = 'none';
                }
            } catch(e) { localStorage.removeItem(storageKey); }
        }

        function createCommentElement(c) {
             try {
                 var deleted = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(removedKey) || '[]');
                 if (deleted.indexOf(c.id) !== -1 || deleted.indexOf(String(c.id)) !== -1) return null;
             } catch(e) {}

             var article = document.createElement('article');
             article.className = 'crki-feedback';
             article.dataset.cid = c.id;
             
             var flagHtml = c.flag ? '<span class="crki-feedback__flag">' + cleanHtml(c.flag) + '</span> ' : '';
             var badgeHtml = c.status === 'pending' ? '<span class="crki-feedback__badge">' + cleanHtml(queueState) + '</span>' : '';
             
             var html = '';
             
             // Header construction based on layout
             html += '<header class="crki-feedback__header">';
             if (dateLayout === 'header_inline') {
                  html += '<span class="crki-feedback__author">' + flagHtml + cleanHtml(c.author) + 
                          '<span class="crki-feedback__date-inline"> ' + cleanHtml(c.date) + '</span>' + 
                          badgeHtml + '</span>';
             } else {
                  html += '<span class="crki-feedback__author">' + flagHtml + cleanHtml(c.author) + badgeHtml + '</span>';
                  if (dateLayout === 'header_right') {
                       html += '<time class="crki-feedback__date">' + cleanHtml(c.date) + '</time>';
                  }
             }
             html += '</header>';
             
             if (dateLayout === 'subtitle') {
                 html += '<div class="crki-feedback__subtitle"><time class="crki-feedback__date-sub">' + cleanHtml(c.date) + '</time></div>';
             }
             
             html += '<div class="crki-feedback__content">' + cleanHtml(c.content).replace(/\n/g, '<br>') + '</div>';
             
             if (dateLayout === 'footer') {
                 html += '<footer class="crki-feedback__footer"><time class="crki-feedback__date-foot">' + cleanHtml(c.date) + '</time></footer>';
             }
             
             if (hasAuth) {
                 html = '<button type="button" class="crki-feedback__admin-delete" onclick="modClear(' + c.id + ')" title="Drop">×</button>' + html;
             }
             
             article.innerHTML = html;
             return article;
        }

        window.fetchMoreComments = function(btn) {
            var pageId = btn.dataset.pageId;
            var offset = parseInt(btn.dataset.cursor);
            var remaining = parseInt(btn.dataset.avail);
            
            btn.disabled = true;
            btn.textContent = 'Loading...';

            fetch('/endpoint.php?op=show_replies&item_id=' + pageId + '&offset=' + offset)
            .then(function(r) { return r.json(); })
            .then(function(result) {
                if (result['success'] && result['items']) {
                    var list = document.querySelector('.crki-feedbacks-list');
                    var comments = result['items'];

                    comments.forEach(function(c) {
                        var el = createCommentElement(c);
                        if (el) list.appendChild(el);
                    });

                    // Update offset and remaining
                    var newRemaining = result['left'] || 0;
                    btn.dataset.cursor = offset + comments.length;
                    btn.dataset.avail = newRemaining;

                    if (newRemaining > 0) {
                        btn.disabled = false;
                        btn.textContent = textTemplate.replace('{count}', newRemaining);
                    } else {
                        // Hide button when no more comments
                        btn.parentElement.style.display = 'none';
                    }
                } else {
                    btn.disabled = false;
                    btn.textContent = textTemplate.replace('{count}', remaining);
                }
            })
            .catch(function(err) {
                btn.disabled = false;
                btn.textContent = textTemplate.replace('{count}', remaining);
            });
        };

        function markDeleted(id) {
            try {
                var list = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(removedKey) || '[]');
                if (list.indexOf(id) === -1) {
                    list.push(id);
                    // Keep last 50 deleted IDs to avoid unlimited growth
                    if (list.length > 50) list.shift();
                    localStorage.setItem(removedKey, JSON.stringify(list));
                }
            } catch(e) {}
        }
        
        function clearDeleted() {
            try {
                var list = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(removedKey) || '[]');
                if (!list.length) return;
                
                list.forEach(function(id) {
                    var el = document.querySelector('[data-cid="' + id + '"]');
                    if (el) el.remove();
                });
            } catch(e) {}
        }
        
        // Call immediately
        clearDeleted();
        // And generally on load
        if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
            document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', clearDeleted);
        }

        window.modClear = function(commentId) {
            if (!confirm("Delete this comment permanently?")) return;

            markDeleted(commentId);
            clearDeleted();

            fetch('/endpoint.php?op=staff_clear', {
                method: 'POST',
                body: new URLSearchParams({ 'item_id': commentId })
            })
            .then(function(r) { return r.json(); })
            .then(function(result) {
                if (result['success']) {
                    if (typeof showNotice === 'function') {
                        showNotice(delMsg, 'success');
                    }
                } else {
                    if (typeof showNotice === 'function') {
                        showNotice(result['err'] || delMsg, 'error');
                    }
                }
            })
            .catch(function(err) {
                if (typeof showNotice === 'function') {
                    showNotice(delMsg, 'error');
                }
            });
        };
        
        // Initial Check
        getPendingStatus();
        
    })();
    </script>
